Welcome_Description:
This installs Voice of the Old Republic, a screen-reader accessibility mod for Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (Steam).

The mod lets blind and visually impaired players play KOTOR with any modern screen reader.
Welcome_GameDescription:
The mod patches your Steam or GoG copy of Knights of the Old Republic.

If you don't own KOTOR yet, you can buy it from Steam or GoG. Otherwise click Next to choose what gets installed.
GameLinks_Description: The mod patches your Steam or GoG copy. One of the games you selected could not be found on this PC — you can buy or install it below, then press Continue.

ModdingInfo_Description:
The following components are always installed alongside the accessibility mod. They are required for basic functionality and cannot be turned off.

Use Tab or arrow keys to read each line. Press Next to continue, or Back to cancel.
ModdingInfo_AccessibilityBody: Screen-reader output, keyboard navigation, audio cues. This project.
ModdingInfo_PrismBody: Routes spoken text to the active screen reader. Replaces the older Tolk library. The accessibility mod cannot speak without it. Credit: the Prism project.
ModdingInfo_WidescreenBody: Required for stable performance on modern monitors. Without them KOTOR has hardcoded 4:3 menus, alt-tab lag, and other display issues. Credit: Wogg (UniWS), ndix UR (KOTOR High Resolution Menus).
ModdingInfo_IniTweaksBody: Community-recommended graphics settings written to swkotor.ini: V-Sync on (fixes the 'character stuck after combat' bug on 60 Hz monitors), Frame Buffer off (fixes the 'crash after character creation' issue), Vertex Buffer Objects disabled (stability tweak for some GPU drivers), and FullScreen off (windowed mode for screen-reader compatibility).
ModSelection_Description: These optional mods improve the KOTOR experience. The recommended ones are already enabled; anything left unchecked is an optional extra. Adjust the boxes before continuing.
ModSelection_K1cpDescription: Highly recommended. Fixes hundreds of bugs, softlocks, and quest-breaking issues. Without it, some quests can become unrecoverable mid-playthrough.
ModSelection_CutContentCheckbox: Restored cut content (JDR + Party Conversations on Ebon Hawk)
ModSelection_CutContentDescription: Restores conversations BioWare cut late in QA. Uses your locale's existing text and voice — no English bleed-through.
ModSelection_SwoopDescription: Restores two cut swoop upgrade items that the racing code already referenced.
ModSelection_ThematicDescription: A balance mod rather than a bugfix: companion stats, feats and starting gear matched to their background. Works on every language version. Applies to a new game only.
ModSelection_FootnoteBody: Note on Italian, Spanish and Polish installs: K1CP only ships official translation patches for German, French, and Russian. Italian, Spanish and Polish installs receive K1CP in English — the bugfix text will appear in English even though the rest of the game stays localised.
GameVersion_Description: Which game should the installer set up? Check one or both boxes, then press Next.
GameVersion_K1Checkbox: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (KOTOR 1)
GameVersion_K1Description: Fully supported. Installs the accessibility mod, the base components, and the optional mods you choose in the next steps.
GameVersion_K2Checkbox: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II - The Sith Lords (KOTOR 2)
GameVersion_K2Description: Full support. Checking this box installs the accessibility mod into KOTOR 2 as well: the mod itself plus the speech runtime, two engine patches (4 GB memory, borderless fullscreen), the recommended settings and keybinds, and it offers to download and install TSLRCM, the KOTOR 2 Community Patch and the Tweak Pack first.
GameVersion_NeedOne_Text: Please check at least one game to continue, or press Back to cancel.
K2Prep_NotDetected: No KOTOR 2 (Steam) installation was found on this PC.
K2Workshop_Warning_Format:
Steam Workshop content was found for KOTOR 2:

{0}

Workshop mods override files installed into the game folder, so they break TSLRCM and the Community Patch that this installer is about to install. Please unsubscribe from all KOTOR 2 Workshop items in Steam, then delete that folder.

Continue anyway?
K2Mods_Description_Format:
{0}

These community mods are installed into KOTOR 2 BEFORE the accessibility mod, because they are the foundation everything else builds on. The first three are highly recommended and preselected; the optional extra at the bottom starts unchecked. Important: do NOT use Steam Workshop mods; unsubscribe from any before continuing.
K2Mods_TslrcmCheckbox: TSLRCM 1.8.6 — The Sith Lords Restored Content Mod
K2Mods_TslrcmDescription: Highly recommended. THE essential KOTOR 2 mod: restores large amounts of cut content and fixes hundreds of bugs. About 138 MB download; installs unattended.
K2Mods_K2cpDescription: Highly recommended. Curated community bugfixes on top of TSLRCM. Note: its fix texts are English-only.
K2Mods_TweakPackDescription: Highly recommended. Reverts a handful of TSLRCM restorations that Obsidian most likely cut on purpose, keeping the story consistent.
K2Mods_ThematicDescription: A balance mod rather than a bugfix: companion stats, feats and starting gear matched to their background, instead of the values KOTOR 2 reused from KOTOR 1. Works on every language version. Applies to a new game only.
K2Mods_Footnote_Format: The install order is handled automatically: TSLRCM first, then the Tweak Pack, then K2CP — the order the community's own build documents. If TSLRCM is neither selected nor already installed, the Tweak Pack and K2CP are skipped to preserve that order. Manual TSLRCM download: {0}
K2Mods_NoTslrcm_Text: TSLRCM is not installed, so K2CP and the Tweak Pack were skipped to preserve the correct install order. Install TSLRCM first, then run this installer again to add them.
K2Mods_NewGameHint: Important: start a NEW game. Savegames from the unmodded game are not compatible with TSLRCM.
K2Lang_Offer_KeepsText: Your game's own text stays exactly as it is.
K2Lang_Offer_BringsText: This edition also brings the Russian text table with it, because the game never shipped a Russian one.

TSLRCM was not installed completely. Manual route: subscribe to the TSLRCM Workshop item for your language, copy its content folders — and dialog.tlk if it has one — out of steamapps\workshop\content\208580\<item> into your game folder, then unsubscribe.
K2Tslrcm_ConfirmInstalled_Text:
Did the TSLRCM installation finish successfully?

The installer could not confirm it automatically. The KOTOR 2 Community Patch and the Tweak Pack must only be installed on top of TSLRCM, so if you answer No they will be skipped.

Answer Yes only if TSLRCM's own installer reported success.
K2Tslrcm_AskAlreadyInstalled_Format:
Is TSLRCM already installed?

You did not select TSLRCM, and the installer cannot confirm it on its own: the localized editions are installed as a plain file copy and leave nothing behind that can be detected. It found {0} patched module file(s) in the game folder — an unmodded KOTOR 2 has none.

Answer Yes if TSLRCM is already installed. Answer No and every mod that has to sit on top of it will be skipped.
ManualDownload_Body_Format:
The installer could not fetch {0} automatically.

Reason: {1}

You can still install it — just download the file yourself and hand it to the installer. Everything after that is automatic.

Steps:
1. Press "Open download page". Your browser opens the official page.
2. Download the file there. It is normally called {2}.
3. Come back here and press "Choose the downloaded file", then pick it.

If the file is already in your Downloads folder, a button offering it directly appears below.

Download page: {3}

Note: the installer normally checks a fingerprint on files it downloads itself. A file you fetched from the official page needs no such check — you chose it.

Russian_Detected_Body: Your dialog.tlk is a Russian community translation, so the mod will speak Russian. The Russian accessibility text is a machine-translated first pass and will be improved by contributors over time.
Russian_NotFound_Body:
You chose Russian, but this KOTOR install is not translated to Russian. The mod can speak Russian, but the game's own text will stay in its current language.

KOTOR has no official Russian release. The community translation is by Artyom 'Allard' Andreev, based on the SerGEAnt's Zone of Games localisation. We cannot bundle or download it for you: it is not published under a licence that allows redistribution, and it has no stable download location we could verify.

To get it, obtain the translation from the author's own channels:
  https://vk.com/allardchannel
  http://www.rpgnuke.ru

Install the translation first, then run this installer again. It will detect the Russian text automatically.
Russian_K1cpUntested_Heading: Note on K1CP with the Russian translation
Russian_K1cpUntested_Body: The author of the Russian translation states that the KOTOR 1 Community Patch has not been tested against it. K1CP is still recommended for everyone else, but on a Russian install this combination is untested by both projects. You can leave K1CP enabled, or uncheck it on the optional mods page if you would rather not risk it.
Polish_Detected_Body: Your dialog.tlk is the official Polish localisation, so the mod will speak Polish. The Polish accessibility text is a machine-translated first pass and will be improved by contributors over time.
Polish_NotFound_Body:
You chose Polish, but this KOTOR install is not translated to Polish. The mod can speak Polish, but the game's own text will stay in its current language.

KOTOR was officially released in Polish in 2004 by Licomp Empik Multimedia (LEM), with subtitles only. That release was never sold on Steam or GoG, and its files are LucasArts content, so we cannot bundle, download or mirror them for you.

If you own the Polish retail release, copy dialog.tlk, dialogF.tlk and the contents of its Override folder into your game folder. You do not need to copy its swkotor.exe: the mod does support that executable, but the Steam and GoG one works just as well for Polish text, and Steam restores its own copy anyway.

Install the Polish text first, then run this installer again. It will detect it automatically.

Main_UnsupportedBuild_Format:
This copy of {0} is not a build the mod supports. Nothing on your PC has been changed.

The mod is matched to the exact program file of each supported release, and this {1} (fingerprint {2}) is not one of them.

The two usual causes:
1. Another mod has already modified {1}. Restore the original — on Steam via Properties, Installed Files, Verify integrity of game files; on GoG by reinstalling — and run this installer again.
2. It is a release the mod does not cover yet.

If your game is unmodified, please report this with the fingerprint above so the build can be added.
Main_ApplyFailed_Format:
The patch could not be installed:

{0}

If the message above mentions a hash mismatch or 'does not support detected game version', your swkotor.exe is a variant we have not seen before. Supported variants in v0.1 are Steam 1.0.3 and GoG 1.0.3 (including byte-equivalent CD re-packs). The Aspyr mobile / macOS port and pre-modified executables (UniWS, HR Menus) are not supported in v0.1.

Please file an issue at https://github.com/JeanStiletto/voice-of-the-old-republic/issues with the displayed hash and we will add your variant if its bytes match.

If the failure happened during the patch step itself rather than the version check, your swkotor.exe may need to be restored. Use Steam's 'Verify integrity of game files' (right-click KOTOR → Properties → Installed Files) or reinstall from GoG.

Main_LoaderBlocked_Format:
The mod is almost fully installed, but the final loader file could not be written:

{0}

This file (dinput8.dll) was blocked — almost always by antivirus or Windows Defender. The mod uses it to load itself when the game starts, and its name matches a pattern that security software often flags by mistake. Your game files are safe and unchanged.

To finish the installation:

1. Open your antivirus (or Windows Security) and add an exclusion for the game folder:
{1}

2. If you use Windows Security, also check Ransomware protection, then Controlled folder access, and either turn it off or allow this installer through.

3. Run this installer again. It will re-apply cleanly.

If the problem continues, temporarily disabling real-time protection during the install usually works. You can turn it back on afterwards.

SpatialAudio_EnabledMessage:
Spatial audio is now ENABLED.

The dsoal DirectSound wrapper and OpenAL Soft renderer have been placed in the game folder, and EAX has been turned on in swkotor.ini. Per-source HRTF spatialization and EAX environmental reverb are now active.

Uninstall_Title: Voice of the Old Republic - Uninstall
Uninstall_Heading: Uninstall Voice of the Old Republic
Uninstall_Description: This removes the accessibility mod's own files only. K1CP and any other optional mods you installed alongside the mod stay in place. To return to fully vanilla KOTOR, verify game files via Steam or reinstall from GoG after this uninstall finishes.
Uninstall_Confirm_Format:
Are you sure you want to remove Voice of the Old Republic from {0}?

This will:
- Remove the mod and the speech runtime (the patches folder)
- Remove the patcher files from the game folder
- Restore the intro logo movies
- Restore the game's own movement keybinds
- Turn off crash-dump capture for {1}
- Remove the Add/Remove Programs entry

What is NOT removed:
- Community mods you installed here (TSLRCM, the Community Patches, the Tweak Pack) stay in place. Each has its own uninstaller.
- {1} keeps its engine patches. Steam's 'Verify integrity of game files' restores it.
- Your save games are untouched.

Note: verifying game files does NOT delete extra files that mods added to the Override folder. For a truly clean game you also have to empty that folder yourself.
Uninstall_Complete_Text: Voice of the Old Republic has been removed.
